sense: a written account kept for later

terms.comment: Properly writing tablets, then anything written on them: accounts, lists, registers and the public records (tabulae pūblicae). See document.

evidence: Cic. Att. 7.3.7: in commentārium (Lewis & Short, s.v. referō)
terms.comment: A private record: notes kept for oneself, a day-book; in the plural also memoirs (Caesar’s Commentāriī).
The record of what was done, especially the official gazette (ācta diurna) and minutes.

phrases.english: the man who reads from the public records

vinyl.html: A gramophone record (“a vinyl record”) is orbis phōnographicus in Traupman 53; that sense has no record here.

acta.html: The neuter plural of āctus, from agō: Gell. 9.6.3 reports āctitō with a long vowel, as from āctus.

sources: Lewis & Short: tabula · Lewis & Short: commentarius · Lewis & Short: ago
